question: Should experimental Claw lifecycle diagnostics be a core Doctor responsibility, and should this stacked slice be accepted after the MCP-ownership prerequisite lands?
rationale: The patch is intentionally gated and well-proven, but it establishes a new core diagnostic boundary over lifecycle ownership, state, source configuration, and live Gateway inventory; that ownership choice cannot be inferred from tests alone.

options.title: Sponsor the gated core diagnostic
options.body: Accept the experimental core Doctor direction, require the small gate-documentation correction, and land after the MCP-ownership prerequisite.

options.title: Keep diagnostics outside core Doctor
options.body: Decline this core surface and direct any future lifecycle inspection toward the owner-specific experimental workflow or an external plugin/skill boundary.

options.title: Pause the stack for RFC resolution
options.body: Wait for the Claws RFC and earlier ownership slices to settle before deciding whether Doctor should own this projection.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the gated core diagnostic
recommendation.body: Accept the experimental core Doctor direction, require the small gate-documentation correction, and land after the MCP-ownership prerequisite.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline provides an explicit review-routing signal, although code-history ownership could not be established from the available read-only inspection.
